subject: POC: Model selection & trial plan
messages:
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rodriguez <alex@acmeinc.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed POC plan (model selection)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the POC: 

Call highlights:
- Goal: Improve customer support deflection and summarization for multi-lingual tickets (EN/ES/FR).
- Primary metric: end-to-end automation rate + human review time reduction.
- Constraints: ramp quickly with open models, low latency for 3k daily requests, data residency in US.

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks):
1) Dataset: 1k sampled tickets across EN/ES/FR provided by Acme, mask PII.
2) Models for evaluation: start with Open LLaMA-2-13B tuned to instruction format (baseline), try Mistral-instruct-13B as low-latency alternative, and a smaller distilled fallback (7B quantized) for cost-sensitive routes.
3) Success criteria (suggested):
   - Precision of automated resolution suggestions >= 85% on sampled evals,
   - Avg latency (99th) < 450ms for EN requests on Dedicated node,
   - Multi-lingual F1 (ES/FR) within 10% of EN baseline.
4) Ownership: Ben (commercial) owns timelines and acceptance; Marissa (SE) will run model tests and perf tuning; Laura will coordinate legal/POC access.
5) Timeline: kick-off next Mon (2026-08-16), data delivery by Tue (2026-08-17), first model runs by Thu (2026-08-19), internal review Fri.

Attachments: I attached a one-page POC checklist and our model recommendation summary.

Next step: Confirm the kickoff date and who will be the primary technical contact at Acme (you or Priya?).

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-08-09T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed POC plan (model selection)

Thanks Ben — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifying Qs:

1) For the multilingual requirement, do you recommend fine-tuning the same 13B model on our Spanish and French ticket subsets, or running language-specific smaller models?
2) For fallback, can the 7B quantized model be used for short-form suggestions only, or do you expect it to handle entire summarization flows?
3) Data residency: we'll need the trial to run in the US-only Dedicated environment — is that feasible for the trial period?

I'll be the primary technical contact, Priya will handle legal and procurement. Kickoff next Mon works for us, but Priya needs the SOW or MOA to start internal approvals.

-Alex
Head of Customer Success | Acme Inc.
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rodriguez <alex@acmeinc.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T11:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed POC plan (model selection)

Hi Alex — quick answers from the SE perspective:

- Multilingual: For speed to result I recommend a single instruction-tuned 13B that we prompt-engineer per language. That reduces overhead for parallel fine-tuning and simplifies routing. If we see degradation >10% on ES/FR we can spin up language-specific 7B variants.
- Fallback 7B quantized: suitable for short suggestions and metadata extraction (intent/classification). For full-length abstractive summarization we expect quality drop vs 13B; we can evaluate hybrid routing (13B for long/complex tickets, 7B for short/simple).
- Dedicated US environment: yes, we can provision a temporary Dedicated node for the trial with NDA/Purchase Order in place. Latency target above assumes Dedicated.

I'll attach proposed eval sets (sampling rubric) and the success criteria workbook that maps metrics to pass/fail thresholds.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
